newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian rightists attack minister over milk quotas.
newsitem.headline: Italian rightists attack minister over milk quotas.

text.p: The hard-right National Alliance party said on Thursday it would present a motion of no-confidence in Italian agriculture minister Michele Pinto over his handling of a row with farmers over EU milk quotas.
Farmers have been camping out in the northern city of Milan for the past eight days to protest at heavy fines imposed on them by the European Union for overproduction of milk.
They have lifted their blockade of Milan's main airport, Linate, but say they are ready to close roads again with their tractors if they do not win more concessions from the centre-left government.
Pinto told parliament on Thursday his ministry would offer farmers cheap loans to help cover the fines and compensation for slaughtering cows in a bid to reduce milk output.

But he repeated that the farmers could not avoid paying the 370 billion lire ($235 million) of levies, which fall due at the end of the month, and said the government was not allowed by EU law to pick up the bill.
"Payment of the super-levy...is a foregone conclusion which neither Italy nor Europe can prevent," Pinto said.

The National Alliance party, which forms part of the centre-right oppostion bloc, the Freedom Alliance, told parliament it would present a motion of no-confidence in the minister. A date for the motion was not immediately set.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi held more than five hours of talks with farmers in Rome on Wednesday and has promised to reply to their long list of grievances shortly.

While farmers in Milan said they would wait to hear Prodi's response before deciding whether to block the traffic again, some 300 farmers in the far south of Italy set up a blockade across a main road leading to the coastal city of Taranto.
Farmers complain they have fallen foul of unfair EU quotas which allow them to produce just 9.9 million tonnes of milk a year against Italy's total milk consumption of some 18 million tonnes.
Pinto asked the European Commission this week to raise Italy's quota to 10.5 million tonnes.
